name: skye-elements-registry
purpose: Composable design elements for Skye/Spectacle MCP generation. Elements are referenced by namespace so sources can be combined without turning into a Frankenstein page.

compositionPolicy.rule: Use one primary visual language per page, then add supporting elements only when they serve the same story.
forbidden: Mixing unrelated hero styles from multiple products
Using an asset because it exists instead of because it clarifies the offer
Stacking every animation library on one page
Combining dark luxury, playful SaaS, brutalist, and app UI styles in the same viewport
Treating screenshots, logos, and 3D objects as interchangeable decorations
Claiming advanced open-source tooling without real imports
Reusing the same dark card/dashboard template with a different brand name
Defaulting a changelog, blog, portfolio, proof-note, or editorial surface into an app-first command surface
required: Run design_stack_audit when advanced tooling is required
Run design_performance_audit when advanced motion, WebGL, screenshots, or scroll effects are used

namespaces.skye.core: Foundational Skye/Spectacle palette, typography, spacing, and proof language.
namespaces.skye.luxury: $50K-grade bespoke elements: editorial typography, strategic whitespace, choreographed motion, and singular visual thesis.
namespaces.skye.fx: Premium cursor, scrollbar, neon text, shimmer, and interaction polish.
namespaces.skye.proof: Client-safe proof panels and operator evidence patterns.
namespaces.skye.brand: Logo, wordmark, identity asset discipline, and anti-generic-brand rules.
namespaces.skyesol.reference: Read-only extracted SkyeSol assets and style notes.
namespaces.skye.templates: First-class revised changelog, blog, and portfolio template packs wired into the MCP.
namespaces.client.surface: App-first surfaces, dashboards, command centers, and control panels.

elements.description: A wide first viewport with a singular visual thesis, short support copy, obvious CTA, and one design/proof/media subject. This is the default public-site hero, not an app dashboard.
elements.useWhen: The product needs a premium public, editorial, changelog, blog, portfolio, proof, or brand first impression and must avoid left-column text walls.

elements.description: A wide first viewport with headline across the page, short support copy, obvious CTA, and one explicit command-surface visual.
elements.useWhen: Only use when the user explicitly asks for a command room, dashboard, admin surface, app shell, control plane, or operational console.

elements.description: Revised Magic UI changelog template with Skye MCP chrome, production-ledger release entries, MDX content, and proof-focused timeline structure.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for a changelog, release receipt, production ledger, release timeline, update feed, or proof chronology.

elements.description: Revised Magic UI blog template with Skye MCP chrome, production field-note content, article cards, tags, and editorial proof structure.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for a blog, field notes, content engine, article library, or technical proof narrative.

elements.description: Revised Magic UI portfolio template with Skye MCP chrome, operator profile content, production proof section, and resume/case-study structure.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for a portfolio, operator profile, resume, proof-of-work site, founder page, or case-study index.

elements.description: The app/tool UI is the first screen, with real controls, tabs, status, and workflow density.
elements.useWhen: The user asked for an app, dashboard, database command center, editor, game, or internal tool.

elements.description: A restrained WebGL/Three.js ambient scene: particles, depth, glow, camera parallax, and product symbolism.
elements.useWhen: The product benefits from a sense of living infrastructure or spatial control.

elements.description: SkyeSol alive background: transparent fixed canvas, aurora wave bands, gold/violet/cyan particles, pointer parallax, scanline, grain, capped DPR, and reduced-motion/mobile fallback.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for SkyeSol-style living backgrounds, alive pages, spectacle atmosphere, or command-chamber energy.

elements.description: A scroll-led story that stages signup, setup, proof, handoff, and conversion with one clear action per stage.
elements.useWhen: A buyer must understand a process or trust path before signup.

elements.description: Client-safe trust evidence: checks, receipts, status, timestamps, proof labels, and handoff state.
elements.useWhen: The page needs proof without exposing internal smoke logs or raw debug output.

elements.description: Transparent founder media staged as an authority object, paired with proof metrics and editorial copy.
elements.useWhen: Founder/operator trust is part of the sale.

elements.description: Subtle entrance, hover, and section reveal motion with reduced-motion fallback.
elements.useWhen: Almost every premium page, unless motion is disabled.

elements.description: Pointer-reactive glow/cursor trail for premium pages, with mobile and reduced-motion fallback.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for cursor trail, high-end interaction polish, or spectacle feel.

elements.description: Optional branded scrollbar with an always-visible, slightly opaque neon track and glowing thumb treatment for vertical and horizontal scroll surfaces.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for a visible custom scrollbar, or a long scroll/table/nav experience needs persistent position feedback.

elements.description: Full-page premium browser chrome: Legal Skyes-style neon scrollbar, top scroll progress rail, pointer-reactive glow, scanline texture, shimmer text, and magnetic hover utility classes.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for the legal page scrollbar style, stronger motion polish, neon UI chrome, scroll-progress feedback, or a page that should feel designed instead of merely styled.

elements.description: Glow, shimmer, split-line, reveal, or chromatic text treatments used as hierarchy, not clutter.
elements.useWhen: The art direction needs neon/glowing/premium display text effects.

elements.description: Use browser/app/product screenshots as the actual visual subject when the surface itself matters.
elements.useWhen: The product has a real app, dashboard, website, or generated surface that needs to be shown.

elements.description: A real MP4/WebM reel recorded from actual browser/app workflows and rendered as the first proof subject.
elements.useWhen: The user asks for screenshots animated into video-style proof, the surface needs to feel live, or the copy claims the app does a workflow.

elements.description: Use approved logo, mark, emblem, and wordmark assets before inventing any new mark.
elements.useWhen: Every branded public page, nav, hero, favicon, app shell, or client surface.

elements.description: Desktop/mobile browser screenshots, no mobile horizontal scroll, visible subject, visible CTA, clean public copy.
elements.useWhen: Every generated public page or app surface.

elements.description: Architecturally-scaled display headline with intentional tracking, tight line-height, weight contrast between display and body, and no system font fallback. Hero text at clamp(3.5rem, 8vw, 9rem), letter-spacing -0.02em to -0.04em, line-height 0.9–1.05.
elements.useWhen: Any $50K-grade surface where the headline must read as designed, not defaulted.

elements.description: First viewport with ≥30% negative space. Section padding ≥10rem desktop / ≥6rem mobile. Hero inner padding ≥8rem. Content never touches viewport edge. Grid margins minimum 4rem horizontal. This is the single biggest differentiator between a $5K and a $50K site.
elements.useWhen: Any premium/luxury build. Required for $50K design standard compliance.

elements.description: Elements reveal in deliberate order with custom cubic-bezier easing: headline (i=0, delay 0ms) → subtext (i=1, delay 80ms) → CTA (i=2, delay 160ms) → supporting visual (i=3, delay 240ms). Never simultaneous. Duration 400ms–700ms. Easing: expo-out or circ-out, never default ease.
elements.useWhen: All $50K surfaces and any surface where entrance motion was requested. Required for design_luxury_audit to pass.

elements.description: At least one hover state, cursor treatment, or transition that could not come from a UI kit: magnetic button pull, cursor-reactive glow with custom spring, text-reveal on hover, tilt/parallax surface, or animated underline with intentional draw timing.
elements.useWhen: Any surface targeting $50K quality where premium interactive feel is a requirement.

elements.description: One dominant visual idea drives every decision on the page: a WebGL product object, a founder authority scene, a cinematic proof tunnel, an editorial full-bleed image, or an interactive app surface. Not a list of features. Not a card grid. One idea, fully committed to.
elements.useWhen: Every $50K-grade page. If there is no singular visual thesis, the page is not ready to build.

elements.description: A project-wide CSS custom property for easing that is not the browser default. Use --ease-expo-out: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) or similar. Applied consistently across all transitions. This single change makes motion feel intentional vs. assembled.
elements.useWhen: Every $50K surface. Required for design_luxury_audit choreography check to pass.
